```{r}
#| label: fig-suncheon-map
#| fig-cap: "주요 관광지 위치 — 순천"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)

places <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "선암사 (Seonamsa Temple)",
    "송광사 (Songgwangsa Temple)",
    "낙안읍성 (Naganeupseong Folk Village)",
    "순천만 갈대밭 (Suncheon Bay Reed Fields)"
  ),
  lat = c(34.99646, 35.00190, 34.90694, 34.87208),
  lng = c(127.33091, 127.27560, 127.33889, 127.51743)
)

leaflet(places) |>
  addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap") |>
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~lng,
    lat = ~lat,
    label = ~name,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>", name, "</b><br>",
      "위도: ", lat, "<br>",
      "경도: ", lng
    )
  ) |>
  fitBounds(
    lng1 = min(places$lng) - 0.01,
    lat1 = min(places$lat) - 0.01,
    lng2 = max(places$lng) + 0.01,
    lat2 = max(places$lat) + 0.01
  )

```


It is a rare in life when one is the giver and recipient of pay forward concept.

It is rare for the giver and the recipient to be the same person in pay forward concept

At the turn of the century, I was working in an industrial complex with well known names like LG and Samsung nearby.

We had bought a leading Korean manufacturer of medical devices and I was in Korea helping with upgrading facilities and integrating the organization into the global operations

---

Rarely do we get to be both the giver and the recipient in the act of paying it forward
